To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mammary uptake of intravenously infused fatty acids is reduced with increased chain lengths and unsaturation and that the mammary gland is the primary site for the incorporation of long-chain polyenoic fatty acids into milk.

intravenous TAG emulsion infusions of long-chain fatty acids were not well transferred into milk fat, and the mammary uptake of long-chain fatty acid TAG emulsion infusates was reduced with increasing chain length and degree of unsaturation.
intravenous infusion of TAG emulsions containing n-3 fatty-acid enriched TAG emulsions increased plasma and milk n-3 fatty acyl concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of long-chain fatty acids to the mammary tissue.
the mammary uptake of intravenous fatty acids.
the transfer of long-chain fatty acids from blood to milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mammary gland is not an effective site for increasing milk fat concentrations of very long-chain n -3 fatty acids.
the mammary gland is not an effective target for increasing n-3 fatty acyls in milk.
the mammary gland is not an efficient organ for uptake of fatty acids from plasma TAG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver regulates the transfer of long-chain fatty acids to the mammary, with the mammary gland having a role to regulate the transfer of fatty acids from blood to milk.
the mammary gland has limited ability to utilize fatty acids from TAG emulsions, and this ability is reduced as chain length and unsaturated increase.
intravenously infused fatty acids are primarily delivered to the mammary glands as FFA and are esterified into TAG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mammary gland does not have the capacity to efficiently transfer fatty acids of longer chain length and greater unsaturation to the milk.
mammary uptake of long-chain poly-unsaturates is limited and is not likely to be improved by intravenous delivery.
mammary uptake of n-3 PUFA was low and that this was not related to the degree of unsaturation of these fatty acids.
